subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following solutions will have the lowest freezing point in water? (2026 Board)
explanation: Freezing point depression depends on the total number of particles (van't Hoff factor i). CaCl2 dissociates into 3 ions (i=3), giving the largest depression and hence the lowest freezing point.
whyWrong: Glucose is a non-electrolyte (i=1), giving the smallest depression.
KCl dissociates into only 2 ions (i=2), less depression than CaCl2.
Urea is a non-electrolyte (i=1), giving the smallest depression.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following is not a transition metal? (2026 Board)
explanation: Sc3+ has a d0 configuration (no partially filled d-orbital in its common oxidation state), so scandium does not show typical transition metal behaviour.
whyWrong: Ag shows a partially filled d-orbital in some oxidation states and typical transition behaviour.
Hg is conventionally excluded as a 'typical' transition element in some texts, but among these options Sc is the standard NCERT answer since Sc3+ is d0.
Cu (3d10 4s1) shows partially filled d-orbital in Cu2+ (3d9) and is a classic transition metal.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following represents the fraction of molecules with energies equal to or greater than Ea? (2026 Board)
explanation: From the Arrhenius equation, k = Ae^(−Ea/RT); the factor e^(−Ea/RT) gives the fraction of molecules having energy equal to or greater than the activation energy Ea.
whyWrong: This is just an exponent, not a fraction of molecules.
This is just an exponent, not a fraction of molecules.
This would represent an unphysical fraction greater than 1 as T increases.

subject: Chemistry
text: What will happen during the electrolysis of aqueous solution of CuCl2 by using platinum electrodes? (2026 Board)
options: H2 gas will be released at cathode
O2 gas will be released at anode
Cl2 gas will be released at anode
explanation: In electrolysis of aqueous CuCl2 with inert Pt electrodes, Cu2+ is preferentially reduced and deposits at the cathode, while Cl− is preferentially oxidised (over water) and Cl2 gas is released at the anode.
whyWrong: Cu deposits at the cathode, not the anode.
Cu2+ is preferentially reduced over H+, so Cu (not H2) is released at the cathode.
Cl− is preferentially oxidised over water at reasonable concentrations, so Cl2, not O2, evolves at the anode.

subject: Chemistry
text: Aspirin is obtained by acetylation of (2026 Board)
explanation: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is prepared by acetylating the -OH group of salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) with acetic anhydride.
whyWrong: Acetylation of phenol gives phenyl acetate, not aspirin.
Salicylaldehyde has a -CHO group, not the carboxylic acid needed for aspirin.
Benzoic acid has no -OH group to acetylate.

subject: Chemistry
text: The secondary valency of Co in the complex [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]2+ is (2026 Board)
explanation: Secondary valency equals the coordination number. Co is bonded to 5 NH3 and 1 NO2− ligand, giving a coordination number (secondary valency) of 6.
whyWrong: 5 is the number of NH3 ligands only, not the total coordination number.
This is the total number of donor atoms bonded to Co (5 NH3 + 1 NO2−) = 6, the coordination number.

subject: Chemistry
text: At low temperature, phenol reacts with dil. HNO3 to yield (2026 Board)
explanation: -OH is an o,p-director; at low temperature with dilute HNO3, phenol undergoes mononitration to give a mixture of ortho- and para-nitrophenol, which are separated by steam distillation.
whyWrong: 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid) requires concentrated HNO3/H2SO4, not dilute HNO3 at low temperature.
Only a fraction of product is ortho; para is also formed.
Only a fraction of product is para; ortho is also formed.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following is 'not' true about enantiomers? (2026 Board)
options: They have the same chemical reactivity.
They have the same specific rotation.
They have the same melting or boiling point.
They have the same refractive index.
explanation: Enantiomers rotate plane-polarised light by equal magnitude but in opposite directions, so their specific rotations are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign, not 'the same'.
whyWrong: This is true; enantiomers react identically with achiral reagents.
This is true; physical properties like m.p./b.p. are identical for enantiomers.
This is true; refractive index is identical for enantiomers.

subject: Chemistry
text: Aniline on direct nitration yields (2026 Board)
explanation: Direct nitration of aniline (with conc. HNO3/H2SO4) partially forms the anilinium ion, which is meta-directing; the mixed effect gives roughly 51% ortho, 47% para and only about 2% meta product.
whyWrong: This reverses the correct major/minor product proportions.
This reverses the correct major/minor product proportions.
Meta is the minor product (~2%), not 47%.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following amines has lowest pKb value? (2026 Board)
explanation: Among aromatic amines, N,N-dimethylaniline is the strongest base (lowest pKb) in this series because the electron-donating methyl groups on nitrogen increase electron density despite steric/resonance effects, and it is most basic compared to the mono-methyl and unsubstituted anilines.
whyWrong: This is less basic than the N,N-dimethyl derivative.
Aniline is less basic than its N-alkylated derivatives here.
Diphenylamine is much less basic due to extensive delocalisation of the lone pair into two rings.

subject: Chemistry
text: The deficiency of which of the following vitamins causes increased fragility of red blood cells and muscular weakness: (2026 Board)
explanation: Vitamin E is an antioxidant that protects cell membranes, including RBC membranes; its deficiency causes increased fragility of red blood cells (haemolysis) and muscular weakness.
whyWrong: Vitamin A deficiency mainly causes night blindness (xerophthalmia).
Vitamin K deficiency causes impaired blood clotting.
Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia (bone disorders).

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): It is not possible to separate the components of an azeotrope by fractional distillation. Reason (R): Components of an azeotrope have the same composition in liquid and vapour phase and boil at a constant temperature. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: An azeotrope boils at constant temperature with identical liquid and vapour compositions, so fractional distillation (which relies on composition differences between phases) cannot separate its components — R correctly explains A.
whyWrong: Both statements are true.
Both statements are true; A is correct.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): The presence of -OH group in phenols directs the incoming group to meta position in the ring. Reason (R): -OH group in phenols activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution reaction. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: -OH is actually an ortho,para-director (not meta), because it activates the ring and donates electron density most strongly to ortho/para positions through resonance. So A is false, while R (that -OH activates the ring towards electrophilic substitution) is true.
whyWrong: A is false: -OH directs to ortho/para, not meta.
A is false.
A is false, not true.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): Actinoids show wide range of oxidation states. Reason (R): Actinoids are radioactive in nature. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Actinoids do show a wide range of oxidation states (due to comparable energies of 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals) and are indeed radioactive — both statements are true, but radioactivity is not the reason for their variable oxidation states.
whyWrong: R does not explain A; the variable oxidation states arise from comparable orbital energies, not radioactivity.
Both A and R are true.
A is true, not false.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with H2N-OH. Reason (R): It indicates the presence of free -CHO group in glucose. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Glucose pentaacetate indeed does not react with hydroxylamine (A is true), but this fact actually indicates the ABSENCE of a free -CHO group (since it is acetylated/blocked), not its presence — so R is false.
whyWrong: R is false, so it cannot be the correct explanation.
A is true, not false.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following is most basic? (2026 Board)
explanation: As the oxidation state of a metal decreases, the metal-oxygen bond becomes more ionic and the oxide becomes more basic. MnO has the lowest oxidation state of Mn (+2) among these, so it is the most basic oxide.
whyWrong: Mn2O7 (+7) is a covalent, strongly acidic oxide.
MnO2 (+4) is amphoteric.
Mn2O3 (+3) is less basic than MnO (+2), being closer to amphoteric character.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following solutions will have the highest osmotic pressure? (2026 Board)
explanation: Osmotic pressure depends on the total particle concentration (van't Hoff factor i). CaCl2 dissociates into 3 ions (i=3), giving the highest effective particle concentration and hence the highest osmotic pressure.
whyWrong: KCl dissociates into only 2 ions (i=2), less than CaCl2.
Glucose is a non-electrolyte (i=1), giving the lowest osmotic pressure.
Urea is a non-electrolyte (i=1), giving the lowest osmotic pressure.

subject: Chemistry
text: For a reaction: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3, the rate of reaction with respect to NH3 is (2026 Board)
explanation: For a reaction with stoichiometric coefficients, rate = (1/coefficient) × (rate of change of concentration). Since NH3 is a product with coefficient 2, Rate = +(1/2) Δ[NH3]/Δt.
whyWrong: The coefficient of NH3 is 2, not 1/3, and it should be divided by, not multiplied.
The rate should be positive (NH3 is a product being formed) and use coefficient 2 correctly as (1/2), but with a positive sign, not negative.
This does not correspond to any correct stoichiometric factor for NH3.

subject: Chemistry
text: How many Faradays are required to reduce 1 mol of Cr2O7^2− to Cr3+ in acidic medium? (2026 Board)
explanation: In Cr2O7^2− → 2Cr3+, each Cr goes from +6 to +3, a gain of 3 electrons per Cr, and there are 2 Cr atoms, so 6 electrons (6 Faradays) are required per mole of Cr2O7^2−.
whyWrong: This is too few electrons for the 2 Cr atoms undergoing a 3-electron reduction each.
This accounts for only one Cr atom's electron change.
This does not match 2 × 3 electrons required.

subject: Chemistry
text: The secondary valency of Pt in [Pt(en)2Cl2]2+ is (2026 Board)
explanation: Secondary valency equals coordination number. Ethylenediamine (en) is bidentate, so 2 en ligands contribute 4 donor atoms, plus 2 Cl− ligands contribute 2 more, giving a total coordination number of 6.
whyWrong: This only counts 2 donor atoms from en incorrectly.
This counts only the Cl ligands, ignoring that en is bidentate.

subject: Chemistry
text: (CH3)3C-OC2H5 on reaction with HI gives (2026 Board)
explanation: Cleavage of this unsymmetrical ether by HI follows SN1 for the tertiary alkyl part (forms a stable 3° carbocation, giving (CH3)3C-I) and SN2 for the primary ethyl part is not favoured on that side because the iodide attacks the more stable tertiary carbon; the oxygen stays with the ethyl group giving C2H5-OH along with (CH3)3C-I.
whyWrong: The ethyl part does not get iodinated when a tertiary carbocation pathway is available.
The reaction does proceed via cleavage, not simple recovery of alcohol/iodide combination given.
This implies no reaction with HI, which is incorrect.

subject: Chemistry
text: An example of non-reducing sugar is (2026 Board)
explanation: In sucrose, both the anomeric carbons of glucose and fructose are involved in the glycosidic bond, leaving no free aldehyde/ketone (hemiacetal) group to reduce Fehling's/Tollens' reagent, making it a non-reducing sugar.
whyWrong: Glucose has a free aldehyde group and is a reducing sugar.
Lactose has a free anomeric carbon and is a reducing sugar.
Maltose has a free anomeric carbon and is a reducing sugar.

subject: Chemistry
text: Benzene diazonium chloride on reaction with phenol in weakly basic medium gives (2026 Board)
explanation: This is an azo coupling reaction: the benzenediazonium ion acts as an electrophile and couples with phenol (activated ring) at the para position (para to -OH) in weakly basic/alkaline medium to give p-hydroxyazobenzene, an azo dye.
whyWrong: Azobenzene would form from coupling two diazonium/amine units without the phenolic -OH substituent pattern shown here.
Simple reduction to benzene is not the reaction occurring.
Chlorobenzene would form via a Sandmeyer-type reaction with Cu2Cl2/HCl, not with phenol.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): The presence of -OH group in phenols directs the incoming group to ortho and para positions. Reason (R): -OH group in phenols activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution reaction. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: -OH is an activating, ortho/para-directing group: its lone pair delocalises into the ring by resonance, increasing electron density most at ortho/para positions and making the ring more reactive towards electrophiles — R correctly explains A.
whyWrong: Both A and R are true.
A is true, not false.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): Actinoids show irregularities in their electronic configurations. Reason (R): In actinoids 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals are of comparable energies. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Because the 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals in actinoids have comparable energies, electrons can occupy any of these depending on the exact element, causing irregular electronic configurations — R correctly explains A.
whyWrong: Both A and R are true.
A is true, not false.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): Components of azeotropes are easily separated by fractional distillation. Reason (R): Components of an azeotrope have same composition in liquid and vapour phase. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Azeotropes cannot be separated by fractional distillation (A is false) precisely because their liquid and vapour compositions are identical (R is true), so there is no composition difference for distillation to exploit.
whyWrong: A is false: azeotropes cannot be separated this way.
A is false.
A is false, not true.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): The two strands of DNA are complementary to each other. Reason (R): The hydrogen bonds are formed between specific pairs of bases. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: DNA strands are complementary because specific hydrogen bonding occurs only between particular base pairs (A-T with 2 H-bonds, G-C with 3 H-bonds), so R correctly explains A.
whyWrong: Both A and R are true.
A is true, not false.

subject: Chemistry
text: In the ring structure of fructose, the anomeric carbon is (2026 Board)
explanation: Fructose is a ketose with the keto group at C-2; on cyclisation, C-2 becomes the new stereocentre (hemiketal carbon), so C-2 is the anomeric carbon of fructose.
whyWrong: C-1 is the anomeric carbon in aldoses like glucose, not in fructose.
C-3 is not involved in hemiketal formation in fructose's furanose ring.
C-5 is the ring oxygen-bearing carbon, not the anomeric carbon.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following is the correct expression of Kf which depends upon the nature of solvent? (2026 Board)
explanation: The molal depression constant is Kf = R·M1·Tf²/(1000·ΔfusH), where M1 is the molar mass of solvent, Tf is its freezing point, and ΔfusH is its enthalpy of fusion — this depends only on solvent properties.
whyWrong: This has ΔfusH in the denominator with wrong grouping, not matching the correct thermodynamic derivation.
This inverts the correct dependence on Tf² and ΔfusH.
This has M1 in the denominator, which is incorrect.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following transition metals has lowest enthalpy of atomisation? (2026 Board)
explanation: Mn has an exceptionally stable half-filled 3d5 4s2 configuration, giving it weaker interatomic metallic bonding (fewer unpaired electrons participate in delocalised bonding) and hence the lowest enthalpy of atomisation among the 3d series metals listed.
whyWrong: Cr (3d5 4s1) has more unpaired electrons and stronger metallic bonding, giving a higher atomisation enthalpy.
V has a higher atomisation enthalpy than Mn.
Fe has a higher atomisation enthalpy than Mn.

subject: Chemistry
text: The secondary valency of Co in [Co(en)3]3+ is (2026 Board)
explanation: Ethylenediamine (en) is a bidentate ligand; with 3 en ligands each contributing 2 donor N atoms, the total coordination number (secondary valency) is 3 × 2 = 6.
whyWrong: This counts only the number of en ligands, not donor atoms.
This is the coordination number: 3 bidentate en ligands × 2 donor atoms each = 6.

subject: Chemistry
text: At low temperature, phenol on reaction with Br2 in CS2 gives (2026 Board)
explanation: In a non-polar solvent like CS2 at low temperature, bromination of phenol is controlled/monosubstitution, giving a mixture of the ortho and para bromophenol isomers (since -OH is o,p-directing).
whyWrong: 2,4,6-Tribromophenol forms with excess bromine water (polar, aqueous), not in CS2 at low temperature.
Ortho product alone is not exclusively formed; para is also formed.
Para product alone is not exclusively formed; ortho is also formed.

subject: Chemistry
text: How does the conductivity vary on decreasing concentration for both weak and strong electrolytes? (2026 Board)
options: It increases for weak electrolyte and decreases for strong electrolyte.
It decreases for weak electrolyte and increases for strong electrolyte.
It increases for both weak and strong electrolytes.
It decreases for both weak and strong electrolytes.
explanation: Molar conductivity increases on dilution for both types (due to increased dissociation for weak electrolytes and reduced ionic interactions for strong electrolytes), but conductivity (specific conductivity, kappa) itself decreases on dilution for both, since the number of ions per unit volume decreases.
whyWrong: Conductivity (not molar conductivity) decreases for weak electrolytes too, as ion concentration per volume falls despite increased dissociation.
Conductivity decreases for strong electrolytes on dilution, not increases.
Conductivity decreases, not increases, for both on dilution.

subject: Chemistry
text: CH3-NH2 on reaction with (CH3CO)2O gives (2026 Board)
explanation: Acetic anhydride acetylates the -NH2 group of methanamine by nucleophilic acyl substitution, replacing one N-H with an acetyl group to give the secondary amide N-methylacetamide, CH3-NH-CO-CH3 (plus acetic acid as byproduct).
whyWrong: This would be the product if ammonia (not a methylamine) reacted with the anhydride.
This is not a correct amide structure for this reaction.
This shows no N-acylation and an unrelated carbon skeleton change.

subject: Chemistry
text: The activation energy of a reaction can be determined from the slope of which of the following curves? (2026 Board)
explanation: The Arrhenius equation ln k = ln A − Ea/(RT) is linear when ln k is plotted against 1/T, giving a straight line with slope = −Ea/R, from which Ea can be determined.
whyWrong: Plotting ln k against T (not 1/T) does not give a straight line related simply to Ea.
This is not the standard Arrhenius linearisation.
This is not the standard way to extract Ea; the Arrhenius plot uses ln k vs 1/T.

subject: Chemistry
text: Identify 'X' in the following reaction: CH3-CO-CH2-CO-O-CH3 --NaBH4--> 'X' (2026 Board)
explanation: NaBH4 is a mild reducing agent that selectively reduces the ketone (C=O) group to a secondary alcohol but does not reduce the ester group, giving CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CO-O-CH3 as product X.
whyWrong: This shows the ester reduced and ketone unreduced, opposite of NaBH4's selectivity.
This shows both groups reduced, but NaBH4 does not reduce esters.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): The presence of -OH group in phenols directs the incoming group at ortho- and para- positions. Reason (R): -OH group in phenols deactivates the aromatic ring. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: A is true: -OH is an ortho/para director. But R is false: -OH is a strongly activating group (increases electron density in the ring via resonance), it does not deactivate the ring.
whyWrong: R is false.
R is false, not true.
A is true, not false.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): Actinoids show irregularities in their electronic configurations. Reason (R): Due to varying stabilities of f0, f7 and f14 occupancies of the 5f orbitals. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: The extra stability of empty (f0), half-filled (f7) and fully-filled (f14) 5f subshells causes electrons to sometimes occupy 6d instead of 5f orbitals, leading to irregular electronic configurations among actinoids — R correctly explains A.
whyWrong: Both A and R are true.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with H2N-OH. Reason (R): It indicates the absence of free -CHO group in glucose. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Glucose pentaacetate does not react with hydroxylamine because acetylation has blocked/used up all -OH groups, and this lack of reactivity correctly indicates that glucose has no free -CHO group in this acetylated form (it exists in the cyclic hemiacetal, blocked, form) — R correctly explains A.
whyWrong: Both A and R are true.
A is true, not false.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): It is not possible to separate the components of an azeotrope by fractional distillation. Reason (R): Minimum boiling azeotrope is formed by the solutions showing large positive deviation from Raoult's law. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Both statements are independently true — azeotropes indeed cannot be separated by fractional distillation, and minimum boiling azeotropes are indeed formed by solutions with large positive deviation. However, R (about how minimum-boiling azeotropes form) does not explain why azeotropes in general resist fractional distillation (that is due to identical liquid/vapour composition at the azeotropic point).
whyWrong: R does not explain A; the true reason is identical liquid and vapour composition at the azeotropic point.
Both A and R are true.

text: Consider the following reaction: Zn(s) + Ag2O(s) + H2O(l) → Zn2+(aq) + 2Ag(s) + 2OH−(aq). Given: E°Ag+/Ag = 0.80 V, E°Zn2+/Zn = −0.76 V, 1 F = 96500 C mol−1. ΔrG° for the above reaction is: (2026 Board)

subject: Chemistry
text: Identify the correct statement: (2026 Board)
options: Molecularity of a reaction is an experimental quantity.
For complex reactions molecularity has no meaning.
Molecularity of a reaction can be zero or even a fraction.
Molecularity more than three is very common in chemical reactions.
explanation: Molecularity is a theoretical concept (number of species colliding in an elementary step); for complex, multistep reactions there is no single overall molecularity, so the term has no meaning for the overall complex reaction.
whyWrong: Molecularity is a theoretical, not experimental, concept (order is experimental).
Molecularity is always a whole number ≥1, never zero or fractional (unlike order).

text: The order for the given reaction is: A + 2B → Products, Rate = k[A]^(1/2)[B]^1 (2026 Board)
explanation: Overall order = sum of the powers of concentration terms in the experimentally determined rate law = 1/2 + 1 = 1.5.
whyWrong: This ignores the fractional 1/2 power of [A].

text: Electronic configuration of chromium is: (2026 Board)
explanation: Chromium is an exception to the normal filling order; it adopts [Ar] 3d5 4s1 to attain the extra stability of a half-filled d-subshell, rather than the expected [Ar] 3d4 4s2.
whyWrong: This is the 'expected' but incorrect configuration ignoring the stability of half-filled d5.

subject: Chemistry
text: The correct IUPAC name of the complex [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] is: (2026 Board)
explanation: Ligands are named alphabetically (ammine before chlorido) regardless of charge type; the complex is neutral overall with 2 Cl− ligands, so Pt is in the +2 oxidation state: diamminedichloridoplatinum(II).
whyWrong: Pt oxidation state here is +2 (balancing 2 Cl−), not +4.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following is heteroleptic complex? (2026 Board)
explanation: A heteroleptic complex has more than one kind of ligand bonded to the central metal. [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ has two types of ligands (NH3 and Cl−), unlike the other three, which each have only one type of ligand (homoleptic).
whyWrong: This has only NH3 ligands (homoleptic).

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following molecules is chiral in nature? (2026 Board)
explanation: Butan-2-ol, CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH3, has a carbon (C2) attached to four different groups (H, OH, CH3, C2H5), making it a chiral centre; the molecule is chiral.

subject: Chemistry
text: Identify the correct increasing order of boiling points of the given compounds: (2026 Board)
explanation: Boiling point of alcohols increases with increasing chain length (more van der Waals interaction) and decreases with branching (branched isomers pack less efficiently and have lower surface area). subject: Chemistry
text: Identify the compound produced by the reduction of Ethanenitrile with Lithium aluminium hydride: (2026 Board)

subject: Chemistry
text: The base which is present in DNA but not in RNA is: (2026 Board)
explanation: Thymine is found in DNA, while RNA contains uracil in its place (uracil lacks the 5-methyl group of thymine).
whyWrong: Guanine is present in both DNA and RNA.

subject: Chemistry
text: Proteins are polymers of alpha-amino acids which are joined to each other by: (2026 Board)
explanation: Amino acids are linked through amide (peptide, -CO-NH-) bonds formed between the -COOH of one amino acid and the -NH2 of another, with loss of water.
whyWrong: Peptide bond is a type of covalent bond, but the specific named linkage here is the peptide bond.
Glycosidic bonds link monosaccharides in carbohydrates, not amino acids.
Coordinate bonds are not involved in amino acid linkage.

subject: Chemistry
text: Which of the following reactions is not explained by the open chain structure of glucose? (2026 Board)
options: Glucose on prolonged heating with HI forms n-hexane.
Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.
Glucose gets oxidized to gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water.
Glucose exists in two different crystalline forms, alpha and beta.
explanation: The existence of two anomeric crystalline forms (alpha and beta) can only be explained by a cyclic (ring, hemiacetal) structure of glucose, not by the open-chain structure, which cannot account for anomers.
whyWrong: This confirms an unbranched straight chain, consistent with the open-chain structure.
This confirms the free -CHO group, consistent with the open-chain structure.
This confirms the free -CHO group, consistent with the open-chain structure.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): The molecularity of the given reaction is 2: 2HI → H2 + I2. Reason (R): Two molecules of the reactants are involved in simultaneous collision between them. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: This is a bimolecular elementary reaction where two HI molecules collide simultaneously to react, giving molecularity 2, which is correctly explained by R.
whyWrong: Both A and R are true.
A is true, not false.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): Zinc, cadmium and mercury are not considered as transition elements. Reason (R): These elements have completely filled orbitals in their ground state as well as in their common oxidation states. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Zn, Cd, Hg have completely filled (n-1)d10 ns2 configurations in the ground state and in their common (+2) oxidation states, so they lack the partially filled d-orbital that defines transition elements — R correctly explains A.
whyWrong: Both A and R are true.
A is true, not false.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): Aromatic primary amines can be prepared by Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis. Reason (R): Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis fails for aromatic primary amines (A is false) precisely because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution (SN2/SNAr under these conditions) with the phthalimide anion, so aniline-type products cannot form (R is true).
whyWrong: A is false.
A is false.
A is false, not true.

subject: Chemistry
text: Assertion (A): Glucose gets oxidized to six carbon gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water. Reason (R): The carbonyl group is absent in the open chain structure of glucose. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: A is true: bromine water mildly oxidises glucose's -CHO to -COOH giving gluconic acid. But R is false: the open-chain structure of glucose does have a carbonyl (aldehyde) group — indeed its presence is exactly why this oxidation occurs.
whyWrong: R is false.
R is false, not true.
A is true, not false.
